New Army Reserve Military Technicians may be authorized moving expenses to their first official duty station. To be eligible to receive moving expenses, you must be a newly appointed Federal civilian employee or have a minimum of a 3-day break in service from previous Federal civilian employment.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the US Army Installation Management Command, US Army Garrison Fort McCoy, Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security Training Division, Range Branch, Range Operations Section located at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Enforce the Fort McCoy Range Safety Program.
Develop a laser safety program.
Review risk assessments for exercises, weapons live and unit operations.
Investigate accidents and incidents that occur during training.
Monitor revisions to AR 385-63 and update Installation regulations accordingly.
Process initial requests for all non-standard training, indirect fire and demolitions.
Develop a current Safety Conflict List for Range Facility Management Support System.
Ensure all safety related data is current in the Range Facility Management Support System.
Develop and update all standard/non-standard Surface Danger Zone, Weapons Danger Zone, Laser Surface Danger Zone, On Range Ammunition Handling Tool safety areas.
Manage UXO mitigation, clearance, reporting within the Training Complex.
Coordinate with Public Affairs on safety matters.
Formulate plans for emergencies in collaboration with Installation Safety Office, Troop Medical Clinic and Protective Services Division.
Direct revision of special instructions in range packets and/or Range Control procedures to enhance training effectiveness and safety.

Must have two years above high school level in business/management or actual food and beverage related work experience of at least two years in a business/management. Must have strong written and oral communication skills, including comprehensive knowledge of standard office software programs, such as word processing, graphics, spreadsheets, etc. Highly Preferred Criteria: All answers to the Highly Preferred criteria must be visible in your resume to get credit. Details.JobSummary: McCoy's Community Center is the central hub of activity. Which includes Dining, Sports Bar, Bowling, Recreation and Leisure Activities and Conference and Catering Spaces. McCoy's Community enter Team provides high-quality service and a place to unwind for the Fort McCoy Community.
Details.SubAgencyName: McCoy's Community Center, Fort McCoy WI
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join the Family, Morale, Welfare & Recreation (FMWR) Team. We proudly serve Military members, Retirees, Department of Defense (DOD) Civilians and their Family. FMWR is the Army organization responsible for delivering quality of life programs to 12 million authorized patrons at nearly 300 military installations in over 30 countries. Careers are available in Child and Youth Programs, Fitness and Recreation, Dining & Entertainment, and Family Services. Service To Country-Join the Army Team and be part of a dynamic organization that directly contributes to the Army's strength and readiness by offering services that reduce stress, build skills and self-confidence, and foster high morale. Travel & Adventure-As a member of the FMWR team, you have the opportunity to grow and expand your career to every corner of the globe. With FMWR you can travel the world and have a fun and rewarding career at the same time. Training & Education-FMWR is a service-focused organization that invests in our workforce and values professional development. As a member of the FMWR team you will have multiple opportunities for professional growth and advancement. Compensation & Benefits-Available employment benefits include competitive starting wages, matching retirement investments, health insurance including vision and dental, generous paid leave, and eleven paid Federal Holidays. More importantly, embark on a career that has endless opportunities and a worldwide network of services.
MajorDuties: Lead a team of business and recreation professionals. Monitors inventory, labor, supply cost, and equipment for the activity.
Responsible for internal control management by providing leadership, supervision, and guidance to ensure attainment of the established business performance objectives.

Directs, develops, and administers plans and procedures, and implements, enforces, and ensures compliance with regulations to provide business operations which meet the needs and interests of the assigned FMWI installation.

Coordinates with Business and Recreation Division Chief for program and funding guidance while preparing a NAF budget and business plan for the facility. Reviews financial reports, estimates projected costs, develops activity financial plan.
Creates marketing and advertising plans for facility. Create and advertise menu to assist catering and everyday operations. Scheduling catering and special events to include ordering product.
Conducts management review of patron programs to identify problems and initiate appropriate corrective measures.
Responsible for overall facility and staff to include scheduling staff.
Other duties as assigned.

Details.JobSummary: National Defense University (NDU) supports the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world.
Details.SubAgencyName: Dwight D. Eisenhower for National Security & Research Strategy
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: National Defense University (NDU) is the premier national security institution focused on advanced joint education, leader development and scholarship. Under the direction and leadership of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the oversight of the Director for Joint Force Development, Joint Staff (J-7), NDU offers a collegial and collaborative academic environment to support the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education (JPME) and other graduate level programs to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world. NDU is comprised of five primary educational institutions and four additional component agencies: National War College (NWC), Dwight Eisenhower School (ES), Joint Forces Staff College (JFSC), College of International Security Affairs (CISA), the College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC), Institute for National Strategic Studies (INSS), International Student Management Office, Operations Support and the CAPSTONE General and Flag Officer Course. NDU has a comprehensive benefits package that includes retirement, social security, and thrift savings plan (TSP); health, life, and long-term care insurance; paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. NDU employees enjoy flexible work schedules, transit subsidy and enhanced telework opportunities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent assesses the communications, logistical, and support requirements for all College activities and ensures full support of those activities.
Coordinates CONUS/OCONUS (foreign and domestic) travel as required to support facility, staff, students and guest speakers.
Engages and negotiates with appropriate support staff elements from the host installation and NDU (higher headquarters) to coordinate required support for all College operations and events.
Performs research tasks and conducts or participates in cost comparison studies of current or projected operations or events. Performs a variety of manpower management review and analysis tasks.
Consults with appropriate University staff manpower on varied issues, procedures and requirements associated with manpower authorizations and personnel actions.

Details.JobSummary: The CHCO/Director (HRD) is the senior expert and principal advisor responsible for leading the management and direction of the NDU HRD, which encompasses the core areas of Workforce and Succession Planning, Competency Management, Talent Management, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, and Executive Support. Ensures the organization's human capital strategy is aligned with current and future mission, goals, and objectives of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Department of Defense (DoD).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The National Defense University (NDU) mission develops joint warfighters and other national security leaders through rigorous academics, research, and engagement to serve the common defense. NDU is organized, operated, and academic/research programs executed under the direction of the NDU President (NDU-P), through the Vice President of Academic Affairs (VP-AA)/Provost and the Vice President for Administration (VP-AD)/Chief Operating Officer (COO), and the Commandants, Chancellors, and Directors of NDU's component organizations. In addition, under the leadership and execution of the VP-AA/Provost and VP-AD/COO, NDU's functionally-aligned and/or matrixed academic and enterprise business support program managers and associated organizations provide University-wide planning and assessment, governance and academic and functional program oversight, strategic and budget planning and programming, human resource management, academic and enterprise business information technology, facilities management, and academic and support services to the mission teaching and research programs. The Provost and COO execute these responsibilities through their respective functional Directorate Heads including the Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO)/Director, Human Resources Directorate (Dir, HRD).
MajorDuties: The CHCO serves as the principal advisor and consultant to the NDU President, Chief Operating Officer and nine NDU Components, on all matters affecting the University's human capital, human resources, and manpower.

The CHCO will ensure that policies and mechanisms are in place to implement the Title 5, Title 10, and military personnel and manpower authorities necessary to meet the human capital requirements of the NDU mission.
The CHCO contributes to formulating and operationalizing the NDU strategic plan in the human capital domain and acts as the Chair of the NDU Human Capital Council (HCC).

The incumbent makes authoritative recommendations for resolving key, critical, sensitive, and controversial human capital issues; the CHCO is dual hatted as the Director, Human Resources Directorate (HRD).

Plans, organizes, directs, coordinates, and reviews the work of the office with full supervisory and management authority for the long range planning, goal setting, and evaluation of subordinate staff.

A selecting official may make selections from the highest quality category (Best Qualified) provided no preference eligible in that category is passed over to select a non-preference eligible in that category unless the requirements of 5 U.S.C. 3317(b) or 3318(b) are satisfied. All information included in the resume and Occupational Questionnaire is subject to review and verification. HR will review your resume and supporting documentation to ensure you meet the minimum qualification requirements. Applicants meeting the minimum requirements will be further evaluated by information provided in the Occupational Questionnaire. If, after reviewing your resume and/or supporting documentation, a determination is made that you have misrepresented your qualifications and/or experience, you may lose consideration for this position and, if you're already an employee, you may be subject to disciplinary action up to and including removal from Federal service.

Details.JobSummary: The CHCO/Director (HRD) is the senior expert and principal advisor responsible for leading the management and direction of the NDU HRD, which encompasses the core areas of Workforce and Succession Planning, Competency Management, Talent Management, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, and Executive Support. Ensures the organization's human capital strategy is aligned with current and future mission, goals, and objectives of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Department of Defense (DoD).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The National Defense University (NDU) mission develops joint warfighters and other national security leaders through rigorous academics, research, and engagement to serve the common defense. NDU is organized, operated, and academic/research programs executed under the direction of the NDU President (NDU-P), through the Vice President of Academic Affairs (VP-AA)/Provost and the Vice President for Administration (VP-AD)/Chief Operating Officer (COO), and the Commandants, Chancellors, and Directors of NDU's component organizations. In addition, under the leadership and execution of the VP-AA/Provost and VP-AD/COO, NDU's functionally-aligned and/or matrixed academic and enterprise business support program managers and associated organizations provide University-wide planning and assessment, governance and academic and functional program oversight, strategic and budget planning and programming, human resource management, academic and enterprise business information technology, facilities management, and academic and support services to the mission teaching and research programs. The Provost and COO execute these responsibilities through their respective functional Directorate Heads including the Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO)/Director, Human Resources Directorate (Dir, HRD).
MajorDuties: The CHCO serves as the principal advisor and consultant to the NDU President, Chief Operating Officer and nine NDU Components, on all matters affecting the University's human capital, human resources, and manpower.

The CHCO will ensure that policies and mechanisms are in place to implement the Title 5, Title 10, and military personnel and manpower authorities necessary to meet the human capital requirements of the NDU mission.
The CHCO contributes to formulating and operationalizing the NDU strategic plan in the human capital domain and acts as the Chair of the NDU Human Capital Council (HCC).

The incumbent makes authoritative recommendations for resolving key, critical, sensitive, and controversial human capital issues; the CHCO is dual hatted as the Director, Human Resources Directorate (HRD).

Plans, organizes, directs, coordinates, and reviews the work of the office with full supervisory and management authority for the long range planning, goal setting, and evaluation of subordinate staff.

Details.JobSummary: National Defense University (NDU) supports the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: National Defense University (NDU) is the premier national security institution focused on advanced joint education, leader development and scholarship. Under the direction and leadership of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the oversight of the Director for Joint Force Development, Joint Staff (J-7), NDU offers a collegial and collaborative academic environment to support the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education (JPME) and other graduate level programs to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world. NDU is comprised of five primary educational institutions and four additional component agencies: National War College (NWC), Dwight Eisenhower School (ES), Joint Forces Staff College (JFSC), College of International Security Affairs (CISA), the College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC), Institute for National Strategic Studies (INSS), International Student Management Office, Operations Support and the CAPSTONE General and Flag Officer Course. NDU has a comprehensive benefits package that includes retirement, social security, and thrift savings plan (TSP); health, life, and long-term care insurance; paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. NDU employees enjoy flexible work schedules, transit subsidy and enhanced telework opportunities.
MajorDuties: Performs technical and procedural administrative support and coordination duties for a NDU College or Component.

Plan, coordinate and integrate administrative activities and procedural functions of the office: daily operational, and administrative duties, and mid-to-long range schedule planning and coordination of academic faculty related events and program.
Interacts professionally with senior members of the military, the government, and academia.
Directly supports an Operations Chief, Chief of Staff, Dean of Administration, or Operations Supervisor in all fact-finding, editing and routing of correspondence, work measurement and processes.
Assists in task studies and analysis activities related to the efficient and effective administration, management, and operations supporting the delivery of an academic program(s) at the University.
Coordinates CONUS/OCONUS travel as required to support faculty, staff, students and guest speakers.
May need to coordinate travel, appointments, passport/visa submission, and logistic support with foreign country and US Embassy officials.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as a Program Manager (Deputy Director) providing professional judgment, initiative, and executive leadership while directing, coordinating, molding, and representing Center of Military History and TRADOC programs and initiatives. Guidelines consist of policy guidance from higher headquarters, DOD and DA regulatory issuances, and applicable Federal and state laws.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: In close coordination with the Executive Director, plans for short and long-term operations for the agency.
Serves as the Deputy Executive Director with direct responsibility for the daily responsibility of an organization.
Ensures actions are consistent with overall direction and resourcing capabilities.
Participates with other managers in setting organizational goals.
Ensures equity of performance standards and rating techniques developed by subordinates.
Coordinates Agency’s annual programming, Planning, Budget, and Execution (PPBES) processes

Details.JobSummary: The College of International Security Affairs' mission is to educate joint warfighters, civilian national security leaders, and partner nation counterparts in critical thinking to inform national strategy and globally integrated operations, under conditions of disruptive change, to prevail across the continuum of competition and war, with a special emphasis on irregular warfare.
Details.SubAgencyName: NDU - The College of International Security Affairs (CISA)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: National Defense University (NDU) is the premier national security institution focused on advanced joint education, leader development and scholarship. Under the direction and leadership of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the oversight of the Director for Joint Force Development, Joint Staff (J-7), NDU offers a collegial and collaborative academic environment to support the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education (JPME) and other graduate level programs to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world. NDU is comprised of five primary educational institutions and four additional component agencies: National War College (NWC), Dwight Eisenhower School (ES), Joint Forces Staff College (JFSC), College of International Security Affairs (CISA), the College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC), Institute for National Strategic Studies (INSS), International Student Management Office, Operations Support and the CAPSTONE General and Flag Officer Course. NDU has a comprehensive benefits package that includes retirement, social security, and thrift savings plan (TSP); health, life, and long-term care insurance; paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. NDU employees enjoy flexible work schedules, transit subsidy and enhanced telework opportunities.
MajorDuties: Principal advisor to College leadership for special events, ceremonies, social functions, programs, and other activities for high-level delegations in support of the College’s research, outreach, and programs for the academic year.
Responsible for event planning and management for ceremonies, conferences, lectures and special events.

Coordinates with co-host and other NDU activities to manage logistical support, security, audio visual (AV), seating plans, escort duties, official honors and coordination with guest and their executive agents, graphics and other support.
Lead event coordinator, in support of College of International Security Affairs (CISA) Leadership, for high-level visits by US and foreign delegations.
Manages the logistics for the College of International Security Affairs (CISA) Chancellor's Lecture Series Guest Speaker Program.
Manages the College of International Security Affairs (CISA) Official Representational Funds (ORF), Student Activity Funds, NDU Foundation Requests and Petty Cash Programs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Applicants must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies or knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. Such experience is typically in or directly relates to the work of the position to be filled. Qualifying experience would be demonstrated by: *Experience developing policies and procedures that optimize the readiness of military and civilian personnel by identifying manpower requirements, personnel placement, and Human Resources requirements. *Experience developing, planning, coordinating, and implementing human capital program requirements in close collaboration with program managers, as well as in conjunction with external human resources (HR) specialists and civilian personnel (CIVPERS) stakeholders. *Experience advising hiring managers regarding duties, responsibilities and requirements for the generation of position descriptions (PDs) including application of occupational structure for work role development; *Experience reviewing and editing PD submission packages from the hiring managers to facilitate classification evaluation and ensure compliance of management principles, classification standards, technical parameters, and conditions of employment with DoD and Navy Cyber Excepted Service (CES) policies; *Experience leveraging expertise in application of human capital theories, principles, policies, and assessment methods to manage and administer workforce programs for FCC cyber, cryptologic, intelligence, space, and information operations civilian personnel; This position is within the Work Category PROFESSIONAL at Work Level SENIOR, Series and Grade GG-0301-13. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://dodcio.defense.gov/Cyber-Workforce/CES.aspx Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will leverage expertise in application of human capital theories, principles, policies and assessment methods to manage/administer workforce programs for FCC's cyber, cryptologic, intelligence, space and information operations civilian personnel.

You will survey wide range of data sources to research and evaluate the efficacy of existing functions and workload distribution, resource allocation, and position validation in supporting achievement of organizational objectives.
You will facilitate the command's implementation of major new human capital initiatives, including Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Personnel System maturation.

You will keep abreast of emerging CES policies and requirements as a CES subject matter expert, advises N1 leadership on the need for new or revised business processes, and advises managers as to effects on their management of workforce assets.
You will advise hiring managers regarding requirements for the generation of CES position descriptions (PDs) including application of the CES occupational structure for work role development.
You will perform duties supporting FCC's CES Delegation of Classification Authority (DCA) which includes assigning appropriate duties and responsibilities to each position.

You will advise hiring managers and senior program managers on how to translate their operational requirements into human capital assets by implementing position management changes in organization designs and defining workforce capabilities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes participating in the implementation of a Financial Literacy program; conducting site visits to promote a Financial Literacy program; coordinating class schedules and assisting with data entry; and conducting training on the use of automated systems. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Organizational Management, Public Administration, Business Administration. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Customer Service Oral Communication Planning and Evaluating Technical Competence

Details.JobSummary: Amended closing date to 1 November About the Position: This position is with the 99th Readiness Command, Family Coordinator Office located at Fort Meade, MD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Conduct site visits to US Army Reserve units to promote the Financial Literacy program.
Brief leadership and staff on Financial Literacy program status to include issues and accomplishments.
Serve as liaison between US Army Reserve units and counselors to facilitate the delivery of the Financial Literacy program.
Assist with the scheduling of Financial Literacy program classes and events.
Engage in work groups to ensure the financial readiness needs of service members are met.
Coordinate the dissemination of program information through the Public Affairs office.
Participate in the strategic planning of the Financial Literacy program within the US Army Reserve Command.
Evaluate Financial Literacy event data to ensure the program goals are met.
Participate in the development of a strategic plan for the Financial Literacy program based on the needs of staff.
Recommend appropriate financial training for personnel based on Vantage requirements.
Administer training on the operation of relevant computer software to ensure program data is entered appropriately.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. This is a GG-13 position in the Cyber Excepted Service (CES). The GG-13 duties for the "Professional" work category are at the "Full Performance" work level and are equivalent to those at the GS-13 level. The selectee's salary will be set within the grade equivalent to a GS/GG grade based on the selectee's qualifications in relation to the job. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: a broad knowledge of and demonstrated ability to apply knowledge of various aspects of Cyber Operations (CO) to plan, manage, and coordinate CO planning projects requiring collaboration with various internal and external components; knowledge of Geographic Combatant Commander (COCOM) CO program roles and responsibilities, as well as COCOMs? use of IT assets to facilitate military operations; and knowledge of and skill in applying the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) and Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP), with emphasis on mission analysis, course of action (COA) development and comparison, and plans/orders development. Note: Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector, or experience gained in another government agency. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Ability to conduct military/contingency and crisis action planning for cyberspace operations. 2. Knowledge of and skill in applying the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) and Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP), IAW JP 5.0, with emphasis on mission analysis, course of action (COA) development and comparison, and plans/orders development. 3. Ability to provide technical knowledge and skill as a military planning specialist. 4. Broad knowledge of and demonstrated ability to apply knowledge of DoD Computer Network Operations (CNO) to plan, manage and coordinate CNO planning projects requiring collaboration with various internal and external components. 5. Knowledge of Combatant Commander (COCOM) cyber program roles and responsibilities as well as use of IT assets to facilitate day-to-day operations. 6. Skill in communicating complex information concerning CNO initiatives, both orally and in writing, to provide effective briefings and reports to senior leaders. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT CONTINUED: This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Testing Program. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. Therefore, incumbent is required to: (a) refrain from the use of illegal drugs, and (b) if requested, submit to urinalysis testing. Incumbent may be selected for random drug testing and may be subject to reasonable suspicion testing and safety mishap or accident testing.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Cyber Excepted Service (CES) position implemented under Section 1599f of Title 10, United States Code (U.S.C). This position is in the Excepted Service. DoD Components with CES positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, CES Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. All new CES employees are required to complete a three-year CES trial period. Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service. For additional information, click here For additional information on CES, click here
MajorDuties: DUTY 1: Serves as a senior future operations planner in support of Cyber National Mission Force operational planning related to its Defend the Nation (DTN) in cyberspace mission. DUTY 2: Coordinates and manages CNMF National Support Teams (NSTs) operational employment to meet CNMF operational requirements in support National Mission Team (NMTs) and National Cyber Protection Teams (N-CPTs) mission execution. Serves as the subject matter expert (SME) for CDR CNMF concerning NST issues. DUTY 3: Develops analytical inputs for CNMF cyberspace plans and operations and produces layman explanations on these technical/ analytical activities. DUTY 4: Attends meetings, conferences, briefings, and seminars related to Cyberspace Operations.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. MajorDuties: -Applying background experience, inputs and maintains relevant information to analyze, develop, and evaluate issues, and to develop detailed plans, goals, objectives, and recommendations to resolve substantive problems and issues of effectiveness and efficiency of work operations for long-range implementation in assigned program areas. Assigned programs support resource allocation, modernization, and force management and analysis, including integrating, coordinating, prioritizing, and advocating USCYBERCOM future concepts, mission capability/resource needs relating to the USCYBERCOM assigned mission areas of cyber space operations and information operations. -Documents planning and programming decisions in appropriate formats, and provides technical guidance and advisor support, to meet USCYBERCOM assigned program requirements. Identifies non-standard or emerging operational requirements, assesses impact on assigned programs, and develops recommendations. Monitors the Command's Workflow Management System (WMS) Database and the Request for Information (RFI)/Situational Awareness Tool, at the direction of the DCoS/CoS, to ensure taskers are assigned to the appropriate J3 division for completion. -Actively participates in strategic planning to improve organizational direction and focus using strategic planning tools and techniques. Prepares detailed plans, budgets, and schedules for assigned major programs and/or participates with management in fiscal planning, programming and advocating. -Conduct contract surveillance in the manner described in the COR Handbook and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.201-7000 to ensure the J3's contractors are providing quality services and supplies in a timely manner, within cost; to mitigate contractor performance problems; and to ensure that the Government receives best value for the Warfighter. Completes required training and maintains COR certifications, consistent with governing federal regulations, and DoD and USAF policy directives; documents satisfactory completion in the COR Tool (CORT).

Do NOT include photographs (or links to social media such as LinkedIn), inappropriate material, inappropriate content, nor personal information such as age, gender, religion, social security number, etc., on your resume. Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD-Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD-Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy/copies of your last or most recent SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action. The SF-50, block 24 must contain "1" or "2" and block 34 must be a"1". Employees eligible under an OPM approved interchange agreement, block 34 may contain a "1" or "2". NOTE: For OCONUS employees who claim eligibility MSP or Family Member Preference, your SF-50 may contain a "3" in block 24 and a "2" in block 34. Promotion Consideration: If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirements. You will need to provide additional SF-50s which clearly demonstrates you meet the time-in-grade requirements (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Promotions, Within-Grade, Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s with an effective date more than one year old). ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt. OPTIONAL DOCUMENTS: Performance Appraisals for Current Federal Civilian Employees - Most recent performance appraisals (dated within last 3 years) showing the official rating of record, signed by a supervisor, or statement why the performance appraisal is unavailable. Awards for Current Federal Civilian employees - List any awards received within the last 3 years on the resume. Note: Applicant must not submit award SF50s-Notification of Personnel Actions (SF50s).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is located in the Defense Media Activity (DMA), a Department of Defense Field Activity reporting to the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Public Affairs) (ATSD (PA)). The DMA is a worldwide media organization charged with informing Department of Defense (DoD) audiences, managing the Department's visual information records, training the Department's public affairs and visual information workforce and providing broadcast radio and television to DoD personnel overseas operating from multiple locations in the United States and overseas, including deployed combat and contingency forces worldwide.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Management Analyst at the GS-0343-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as the Military HR and Manpower Division Chief, responsible for providing guidance on all Military HR Programs to include developing policy, strategic direction and management over all Military matters. Directly responsible for oversight, control and direction of the DMA manpower program and supports in the execution of the activity's responsibilities for manpower management in accordance with DoD directives, instructions and standards. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Advises and provides counsel to military HR staff regarding policies, procedures, OSD directives and internal management instructions. Plans, organizes, and directs the activities of the Military HR Division, ensuring that the advice and assistance provided complies with legal and regulatory requirements and meets the customer's needs. Develops goals and objectives that integrates service requirements into consolidated strategic direction and guidance for all military programs. Reviews organization mission, functions, and manning levels, identifies requirements and initiative requests for additional resources including personnel, equipment, supplies to ensure success in meeting goals and objectives. Provides advice to supervisor on significant issues and problems related to work accomplishment.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 335th Signal Command (Theater), US Cyber Command, Army Reserve Element located in Fort Meade, Maryland. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Monitor unit and individual training requirements through an automated Army training system.
Maintain unit training budget for justified authorizations and efficiency.
Request training for staff in Army Training Requirements and Resources System (ATRRS).
Reviewing training records to recommend individual and unit training.
Draft instructions, requests, reports, and briefings on the status of the program requirements and uniform application.
Develop forecasts and provide input for training plans.
Analyze plans, reports and regulations to determine training needs and recommend program changes.
Review mobilization plans and directives issued by higher headquarters and monitor implementation.
Conduct inspections to ensure training exercises are in accordance with Army Organizational Inspection Program procedures.
Review reports to assure accomplishments of training program objectives are met.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Moore is the Maneuver Center of Excellence and home of the Infantry Division and Armor School. More than half of all new Soldiers who enter the Army will do so at Fort Moore. With the third-largest troop density, Fort Moore is the sixth-largest military installation in the United States. More than 100,000 Soldiers, family members, Veterans, civilians, and contract employees live, work and use services on the installation every day. Fort Moore is located in an area commonly known as the "Tri-Community", comprised of Columbus, Fort Moore, Georgia, and Phenix City, Alabama. Columbus, known as Georgia's third-largest city, is a growing community of 250,000. The stunning Florida gulf shores and picturesque Blue Ridge Mountains are only a few hours' drive from Fort Moore. Responsible for the full range of supervisory duties for a diverse population, to include exercising significant responsibilities in dealing with officials of other units or organizations.

The geography and climate are ideal for year round military training. Public transportation and free parking is available.
Details.SubAgencyName: Directorate of Training and Doctrine (DOTD) Doctrine and Collective Training Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Maneuver Doctrine Writer for the Directorate of Training and Doctrine (DOTD) in the Maneuver Center of Excellence.
Evaluate brigade/regiment and battalion/squadron doctrine and tactics, techniques, and procedures in order to validate, modify, or write new doctrine in support of maneuver missions.
Evaluate combined, joint, multi-service, and Army concepts, doctrine, in order to analyze, validate, modify, or develop and support new doctrine.
Review new systems, concepts, organizations, equipment, and personnel in support of maneuver missions and other activities.
Coordinate with Training and Doctrine Command organizations/field units to review doctrinal and training publications using current products and doctrine concepts and scenarios.
Develop and operate a program for the systematic staffing and reviewing of assigned doctrinal literature to ensure synchronization with current maneuver doctrine, and training programs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or expereince requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1). event planning such as: tours, orientation briefings, receptions, guest speaker programs, and/or other social events. AND 2). Managing volunteer/community outreach programs designed to build and expand relationships between the adult student population and the local community. AND 3). Develop lesson plans for event training. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Public Relations. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is an International Student Program Coordinator, GS-0301-09 Position Located at Fort Moore, Ga.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Moore (Formerly known as Fort Benning) is located in the "Tri-Community" comprised of Columbus, GA; Ft. Moore, GA; and Phenix City, AL. Columbus (Georgia's third-largest city) is home to the 15-mile trail known as the Chattahoochee River Walk. The River Walk provides an excellent facility to bike, in-line skate, jog, or just take a leisurely stroll and enjoy the scenery. Columbus offers a variety of attractions such as the State Theatre of Georgia, the historic Springer Opera House; the National Civil War Naval Museum at Port Columbus; the National Infantry Museum, which displays a large collection of military art and artifacts; the Columbus Museum, one of the largest state-of-the-art facilities in the Southeast; and the beautiful Historic District- circa 1850-1870. The stunning Florida gulf shores and Blue Ridge Mountains are only a few hours' drive.
MajorDuties: Informally brief students on the aspects of tours, to include climate, attire, objectives, duration, and other relevant aspects.

Arrange media appearances and speaking engagements for International Students to expose the U.S. military and local civilian communities to the customs, beliefs, and functions of allied and partner nations as represented by International Student.
Monitor organizational budget to ensure funds are available for International Student requirements.
Provide information and guidance to volunteers and community groups relative to religious, cultural, and social beliefs and customs of different countries.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the Defense Health Agency. It is located within the Southwest Georgia Martin Army Community Hospital Director of Executive Located in Fort Moore, GA. This position serves as the Health Informatics Officer and Chief in a Market level office within the Defense Health Agency (DHA). Provide management, administrative oversight and support to ensure the delivery of integrated, affordable and high-quality healthcare to beneficiaries.
Details.SubAgencyName: DHA SOUTHWEST GEORGIA MARKET, ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPITAL MARTIN, DIRECTOR OF EXECUTIVE
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an integrated health care system, the Defense Health Agency delivers healthcare services across the Department of Defense and enables combat support to the Joint Force as a strategic partner. Through a robust healthcare delivery system, and a dedicated team of inspired professionals, the Agency ensures the worldwide delivery of medical, dental, and pharmacy programs to more than 9.6 million uniformed service members, retirees, and their families, by improving health and building readiness Anytime, Anywhere-Always. The selecting official has requested a competitive and noncompetitive candidate list for this vacancy. If you are eligible for the noncompetitive list, you will be evaluated on basic and/or minimum qualifications, as applicable. While required to answer the assessment questions, non-competitive candidates will not be evaluated against the competitive rating & ranking criteria. The selecting official may select from any of the candidate lists.
MajorDuties: Develop plans, identifies resource needs and prioritizes initiatives with a focus on DHA’s Quadruple Aim Performance Plan (QPP).
Develop initiatives to support data analysis and quality improvements in the areas of health informatics.
Monitor the functionality of health information systems to ensure efficient and effective progress and establish the appropriate metrics to evaluate informatics outcomes.

Ensure the delivery of integrated, affordable and high-quality healthcare to beneficiaries in accordance with DHA’s priorities of great outcomes, ready medical force, satisfied patients and fulfilled staff.
Recommend resolution of issues that affect technical, legal, ethical, financial, informatics, and organizational factors within the Market.
Serve in a leadership position over a large Medical Market within the Defense Health Agency.

Collaborate with all forms of medical staff to ensure that health informatics related concerns, challenges and initiatives are shared and advocated for within the Market and when appropriate with DHA’s Chief Health Informatics Officer (CHIO).
Develop and maintains a close liaison and coordination with other Market’s CHIOs/CMIOs and end users of the clinical information systems.
Evaluate health care situations and apply extensive experience in dealing with and resolving problems.
Identify gaps in performance to support the deployment and adoption of new health informatics capabilities within the market such as a new electronic health record.
Develop quality improvement initiatives in the area of health informatics to improve the efficiencies and effectiveness of current systems/tools.
Support of DHA’s Quadruple Aim Performance Plan (QPP) to identify resource needs and prioritizes initiatives across the Military Health System (MHS).

QUALIFICATIONS GS-09: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes utilizing established procedures in administering scheduled evaluations and inspections to assure conformance with contract; assisting in analyzing requirements and develop recommendations; and/or making guided decisions concerning planning and selecting surveillance techniques, determining adequacy of contractor operations and extent of corrective action. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. QUALIFICATIONS GS-11: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes performing evaluation methods, surveillance plans and techniques, principles, procedures and regulations as related to surveillance of contractor performance; providing advice and guidance to management on contracting methods; conducting review of contracts, contracting plans; and/or applying guidelines to performance problems encountered in service contracts; applying contract policies and procedures to assist the contracting officer in matters related to contract requirements and contract administration; monitoring inspection schedules, checklists, samples and other surveillance technique for compliance with Quality Assurance; and/or analyzing data to detect unsatisfactory trends/conditions weaknesses in contractor performance. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Research and analyze data identifying trends and report results to management.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 9th Mission Support Command, Satellite Alaska, Soldier Readiness Action Center, Theater Support Group located at Fort Richardson, Alaska. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a Military Technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Prepare military correspondence and orders and maintain files.
Prepare military personnel actions including evaluation reports, applications for appointment, promotions, individual orders, retirement point cards, or transfers.
Provide technical advice on establishment and maintenance of pay accounts ensuring compliance with laws and regulations as well as researching complex pay issues.
Assist in developing Standard Operating Procedures ensuring uniform interpretation and application.

Provide guidance on administrative and personnel matters such as recruitment, retention, assignment and transfer, Military Occupation Specialty, personnel strength, discharge, retirement, promotion, discipline, or utilization.
Research and analyze data identifying trends and report results to management.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The incumbent will serve as an Antiterrorism Officer (Garrison) for DPTMS (Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization, and Security) in Fort Riley, KS.
Details.SubAgencyName: DPTMS (Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization, and Security)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Develop crisis management plans in response to potential terrorist attacks.
Protect and secure personnel and property from terrorist activities.
Monitor the core vulnerability assessment program to identify potential liabilities throughout the organization.
Secure funding to meet security and protection requirements.
Provide guidance and training regarding antiterrorism and force protection procedures to personnel throughout the organization.
Details.Education: Education Qualifications for GS-12: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. Education Qualifications for GS-11: Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Criminal Justice. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Work experience managing or directing the activities of the type of business (i.e.; restaurant, bowling center, golf course, or other types of business and recreation programs and facilities) to be managed. Highly preferred candidates will be referred to management first. Highly preferred is defined as meeting all of the criteria listed below: 1). Minimum of 2 years experience in managing or directing any of the following types of businesses: Family entertainment facility, bowling center or other recreation programs, restaurant, or food and beverage operation, as well as supervising staff, to include performance management and training. 2). Experience with financial analysis, budget development and execution, and food/labor cost management. 3). Experience with marketing and executing programs and events. *Highly preferred experience must be clearly stated in resume to be qualified as highly preferred.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at SpareTime Interactive Entertainment. This position is eligible for the NAF benefits package and leave accrual. To better expedite the hiring process, we recommend including full contact information (name, address, phone number, email, etc.) for professional and personal references on your resume.
Details.SubAgencyName: Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: SpareTime Interactive Entertainment is a large amusement complex featuring family friendly dining and entertainment. The 35,000 square foot facility holds 15 lanes of traditional and hyper bowling, batting cages, kitchen, pub, golf and sports simulators, 18-hole glow mini-golf, and OMNI VR Arena. SpareTime is a state-of-the-art facility is available to the community for birthday parties, hail and farewells, unit functions, Garrison events, and daily recreational use. Fort Riley, "Home of the Big Red One" (1st Infantry Division), is known for its excellent training, abundant recreational opportunities, rich history, and tremendous relations with surrounding communities. Fort Riley is in the Central Flint Hills Region of northeastern Kansas, one hour west of Topeka, the state capital, and two and a half hours west of Kansas City. Fort Riley boasts a variety of thriving communities, with the closest being Junction City, Ogden and Manhattan.
MajorDuties: Manages, plans, organizes, and conducts a large business and recreation program.
Formulates instructions and directives necessary to operate a profit generating business and recreation activity.

Coordinates business and recreation programs, activities, and events with community and military representatives. Such activities include, but not limited to, amusement and recreational activities and food and beverage operations.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Employee serve as Director of the Fort Sam Houston/Camp Bullis Mission Training Complex (MTC) and is responsible for supervision and management of the installation's mission command training facilities. This includes direct contract management of the MTC. ***Note: Duty location will be Camp Bullis, which is located approximately 30 miles north of Fort Sam Houston.
Details.SubAgencyName: US Army Support Activity - DPTMS/Training Branch
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Responsible for resource and contractual oversight for the Mission Training Complex.
Direct the work of the organization, tasking contractors and others to perform essential operating functions.
Provide program management oversight and programmatic guidance for contractor personnel assigned to the organization.
Plan, direct, and oversee the mission-essential functions of the MTC.
Assure work practices are followed and that the workforce is properly oriented, trained, disciplined, and counseled.
Develop operational and facility modernization budgets and manage an annual operations and maintenance budget.

Serve as MTC subject matter expert for installation staff sections (e.g., Civilian Personnel, Forces Development, Equal Employment Opportunity, Safety, Inspector General, etc.) concerning inspections, reviews, and coordination.
Coordinate training support with National Guard and Reserve component units as well as other services and foreign allies.
Prepare and deliver briefings on Mission Command Training Strategy, to include cost and use of available technology.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes Office of Personnel Management, DoD, and AF Policies, principles, workforce strategic management, techniques, practices, mission and organizational structure of the force management programs: Manpower, Civilian Personnel, Unit Safety, Unit Security, Unit Training, Privacy Act, Freedom of Information Act, Management Internal Control Tool, Records Management, Asset Management and Government Purchase Card. Geographical and program support for 1,500 civil engineer group civilian/military personnel across 11 JBSA sites with a distance of 60 miles between the largest distance. Programs directly and indirectly support the 502ABW and 266 Mission Partners in the DoD's largest and most complex Joint Base. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of civil engineer functions and impact to installation support. 2. Knowledge of the full range of Federal classification and position management principles, concepts, practices, and techniques and of the basic relationships of the various HR disciplines. 3. Ability to perform in-depth research, gather facts, and use extensive and effective analytical and evaluative methods to accurately assess information and make sound decisions involving complex position management problems. 4. Ability to maintain effective relationships with management officials, supervisors, employees, co-workers and others, to ensure cooperative resolution of problems and provide effective coordination of activities. 5. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. 6. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Provides position management advisory services in dealing with difficult, complex, and often controversial position management issues.

This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD Form 214. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form 214 must be submitted upon receipt. OPTIONAL DOCUMENTS: Performance Appraisals for Current Federal Civilian Employees - Most recent performance appraisals (dated within last 3 years) showing the official rating of record, signed by a supervisor, or statement why the performance appraisal is unavailable.
